title: Blessing of a Yacht on the Belon River

image.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art, Nancy F. and Joseph P. Keithley Collection Gift (2020.110)
image.license: Public domain. Released under the Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access program

altText: A river scene in which water fills much of the canvas. Local women in traditional headdresses stand on the riverbank and watch, and a yacht is on the river.

source.verifiedBy: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access API record (title, creators, creation_date, technique, culture, creditline, description, did_you_know, images.web.url, share_license_status CC0)

context: An oil painting by the French artist Maurice Denis, made in the summer of 1899 while he was on vacation in Le Pouldu, Brittany. The Cleveland Museum of Art notes that water fills much of the canvas and that local women in traditional headdresses watch from the riverbank.

descriptions.k: Look at the big river. Water fills much of this painting. Find the women standing on the bank and watching. What are they looking at? Point to the boat.
descriptions.g12: Maurice Denis painted this scene of a boat on the Belon River in France. The title says a yacht is getting a blessing. Women in traditional headdresses stand on the riverbank and watch. Look at all the water. What do you think is happening, and how do the people feel?
descriptions.g35: Maurice Denis painted this oil scene in summer 1899 while on vacation in Brittany, France. Water fills much of the canvas, and local women in traditional headdresses watch from the riverbank. The title tells us a yacht is being blessed. Look at how the river, boat and watchers fit together. What details tell you this is a special event?
descriptions.g68: Denis made this painting during a summer 1899 vacation at Le Pouldu in Brittany. Water fills much of the canvas, and local women in traditional headdresses watch from the bank. The title points to a blessing, a local ceremony. How does Denis balance the large area of water with the watching figures? Use details to explain what the painting asks you to notice.
descriptions.g910: Denis, a French painter who also made church murals and decorative schemes, painted this Breton scene in summer 1899. Water fills much of the canvas, and women in regional headdresses watch from the shore. How does the large expanse of water change the way we read the ceremony named in the title, and what does the composition suggest about community and place?
descriptions.g1112: Painted during a 1899 vacation in Brittany, this scene by Maurice Denis gives much of the canvas to water, while local women in traditional headdresses watch from the bank. Denis was also a decorator of murals in French churches and a theatre ceiling. How might the composition treat a local ceremony as both observed event and designed surface, and what does the large water area do to that balance?

teacherNote.context: An oil painting by the French artist Maurice Denis, made in summer 1899 while on vacation in Le Pouldu, Brittany. The Cleveland Museum of Art notes that water fills much of the canvas and that local women in traditional headdresses watch from the riverbank.
directions: Ask younger students to find the water, the boat and the women and tell what they think the event is.
Have students paint or draw a local event in their own community from the viewpoint of someone watching.
Ask older students to discuss how an artist visiting a region may show its customs and what choices that involves.
